# Support Incident Requirements Checklist: Support Incident Reporting

**Purpose**: Validate requirement quality for safe support incident reporting,
private GitHub issue intake, native fallback UX, dedupe, and privacy boundaries.
**Created**: 2026-06-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Audience / Timing**: PR reviewer before `$speckit-tasks` and `$speckit-analyze`
**Depth**: Standard high-risk requirements gate

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based
on feature context and requirements. Items test the requirements text, not the
implementation.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all reportable custody states defined tightly enough to decide when `Отправить отчет` is primary versus unavailable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK002 Are secondary and fallback copy requirements complete for offline, backend failure, GitHub failure, missing configuration, and intentionally unavailable support intake? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Spec §US2]
- [x] CHK003 Are success requirements complete enough to distinguish internal persistence from user-visible success requiring a private GitHub issue? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK004 Are all required metadata fields for the diagnostic report documented with safe names, availability behavior, and allowed fallback values? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Data Model §SupportIncidentReport]
- [x] CHK005 Are persistence requirements defined for incident scope, reporter-safe identity, dedupe key, affected count, status, redaction result, and GitHub linkage? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Data Model §SupportIncident]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for support incident action state persistence across app refresh and restart? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "metadata-only" defined with an explicit allowlist and forbidden-content list rather than relying on a vague privacy claim? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Private GitHub Issue Format]
- [x] CHK008 Is the user-visible success number format `CUST-{github_issue_number}` unambiguous for both newly created and deduped updated issues? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK009 Is the required GitHub issue title mask specific enough to prevent agent drift in priority, area, user-problem wording, and problem-code placement? [Clarity, Spec §Private GitHub Issue Format]
- [x] CHK010 Are required and optional GitHub labels specified clearly enough to avoid dynamic labels or unlabeled issue creation? [Clarity, Spec §Private GitHub Issue Format]
- [x] CHK011 Are human-facing Russian messages specified exactly for success, failure, terminal expired, and admin/access-policy cases? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Desktop UI Contract]
- [x] CHK012 Is the phrase "bounded list" quantified consistently as a maximum of 5 safe affected identities across plan, data model, and issue body requirements? [Clarity, Plan §Scale/Scope, Data Model §SupportIncident]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Are desktop, backend, and GitHub responsibilities consistent with the rule that the desktop never creates tracker issues directly? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-014, Contract §Endpoint]
- [x] CHK014 Are the fallback requirements consistent between user scenarios, API failure responses, and desktop UI copy? [Consistency, Spec §US2, Contract §Failure Responses, Contract §Desktop UI Contract]
- [x] CHK015 Are redaction requirements consistent between desktop report construction, server-side validation, storage, logs, issue bodies, and PR evidence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK016 Are dedupe requirements consistent between user story aggregate behavior, data model uniqueness, GitHub issue update semantics, and affected count? [Consistency, Spec §US1, Spec §FR-009, Data Model §SupportIncidentDedupeKey]
- [x] CHK017 Are WebView/cabinet boundary requirements consistent across spec, plan, research, and contract so implementation cannot drift into `cabinet/web.py`? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, Plan §Summary, Research §Desktop API Boundary]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK018 Can each success criterion be objectively evaluated without requesting audio, transcript text, raw paths, tokens, signed URLs, or private meeting content? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK019 Are measurable outcomes defined for GitHub issue format, repo privacy, incident number persistence, dedupe, fallback timing, and WebView non-change? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK020 Are validation expectations traceable from success criteria to focused server/macOS checks without turning the checklist into implementation test steps? [Traceability, Spec §FR-022, Plan §Validation Plan]
- [x] CHK021 Are issue body acceptance criteria specific enough for a future triage agent to classify privacy, custody state, data-loss risk, and ownership path? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §Private GitHub Issue Format, Spec §SC-009]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are primary, duplicate, aggregate, failure, and support-review scenarios all represented as independently testable requirement narratives? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [x] CHK023 Are exception paths specified for unsafe payloads, malformed metadata, unsupported schema versions, missing labels, wrong repo, public repo, GitHub unavailability, and rate limiting? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Failure Responses]
- [x] CHK024 Are recovery or retry expectations defined for internally retained incidents when GitHub creation is unavailable but user-visible success is not allowed? [Coverage, Spec §US3, Data Model §State Transitions]
- [x] CHK025 Are cross-tenant and identity-change scenarios specified clearly enough to prevent sending reports into the wrong workspace? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK026 Are terminal expired cases with `server_identity_present=false` and `local_media_retained=true` fully specified in both user copy and metadata requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK027 Are admin/access-policy blockers described with enough requirement detail to route support/admin ownership without exposing internal enum codes as primary explanation? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK028 Are duplicate-send and already-accepted incident requirements specific enough to prevent user-visible issue spam? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-009]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK029 Are privacy/security requirements complete for payloads, persistence, GitHub bodies, logs, tests, screenshots, support exports, and PR evidence? [Security, Spec §FR-018, Plan §Constraints]
- [x] CHK030 Are external dependency requirements specified for GitHub authentication, repo privacy confirmation, label validation, timeouts, rate limits, and degraded fallback? [Dependency, Spec §Private GitHub Issue Format, Research §GitHub Issue]
- [x] CHK031 Are performance/degraded-state requirements quantified enough for offline or unavailable support intake to avoid hanging the user flow? [Performance, Spec §SC-008, Plan §Performance Goals]
- [x] CHK032 Are accessibility and localization requirements explicit enough for all native support report actions and status messages, beyond the presence of Russian copy? [Gap, Plan §Constitution Check]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK033 Are assumptions about `yshishenya/crisp` being private, label availability, and future issue-triage agent processing documented as requirements or configuration gates? [Assumption, Spec §Clarifications, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK034 Are migration and lifecycle assumptions documented for retaining full safe metadata indefinitely while still allowing manual redaction for privacy/security incidents? [Assumption, Spec §FR-017, Data Model §PrivateGitHubIssue]
- [x] CHK035 Are backend storage and GitHub issue dependencies described with enough boundary detail to keep server-owned WebView list ownership separate from support intake? [Dependency, Plan §Project Structure, Research §Desktop API Boundary]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK036 Is the relationship between `problem_code`, `failure_category`, `retry_class`, root-cause fingerprint, and dedupe key defined clearly enough to avoid incompatible dedupe implementations? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009, Data Model §SupportIncidentDedupeKey]
- [x] CHK037 Is the v1 policy for human-identifying names/emails explicit enough to forbid them and require safe ids or fingerprints instead? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK038 Are fallback messages and support issue sections free of any promise to restore a recording unless restoration is independently proven? [Conflict, Spec §US2, Spec §Private GitHub Issue Format]
